claim: llm-d-router ships a documented, working 'multi-cluster variant' plugin family (multicluster-file-discovery, multicluster-metrics-data-source, multicluster-metrics-extractor, multicluster-kv-cache-utilization-scorer, multicluster-queue-scorer, multicluster-session-affinity-filter, multicluster-prefix-cache-scorer, multicluster-approx-prefix-cache-producer) for a cluster-scoped EPP whose 'candidate endpoints are clusters' instead of pods -- a direct, shipping precedent for non-pod-backend routing.
stance_target: existence of an already-implemented non-pod-backend routing pattern in llm-d-router
quoted_support: A few plugins ship a multi-cluster variant beside the stock plugin, for a cluster-scoped EPP whose candidate endpoints are clusters.

claim: The multicluster-file-discovery plugin's config file (clusters.yaml) 'follows the same format as the pod file discovery, except an address may be a hostname' -- i.e. the EPP's own endpoint-discovery abstraction already supports hostname-based (non-pod-IP) addressing as an alternative input, configured purely via YAML (dataLayer.discovery.endpoints.pluginRef), with no core-code change required to point the EPP at non-Kubernetes-pod endpoints.
stance_target: the central research question: can the EPP's discovery/backend model support non-k8s-pod addressed endpoints
quoted_support: clusters.yaml follows the same format as the pod file discovery, except an address may be a hostname.

claim: The multicluster scorers are not standalone -- multicluster-kv-cache-utilization-scorer and multicluster-queue-scorer depend on pool-aggregate metrics written by multicluster-metrics-extractor from data scraped by multicluster-metrics-data-source, and a config with the scorers but without the matching source+extractor fails to load, revealing an implicit plugin-dependency contract enforced at config-load time rather than via typed interfaces.
stance_target: operational constraint: plugin combinations must be internally consistent or the EPP refuses to start
quoted_support: The metric scorers are not standalone. ... Configure all three together in dataLayer. A config with the scorers but without the source and extractor fails to load.

claim: Every plugin is assigned a Stability Level (Alpha/Beta/Stable) at registration, and cmd/epp/runner/runner.go is 'the single source of truth for in-tree plugin stability' -- confirming plugin registration happens in Go source at a specific, named file, not via a config-driven registry.
stance_target: how plugins are registered -- pinpointing the exact compile-time registration location
quoted_support: Every plugin in llm-d-router is assigned a Stability Level upon registration (cmd/epp/runner/runner.go is the single source of truth for in-tree plugin stability)

claim: Alpha-stability plugins require the EPP process to be launched with --allow-experimental-plugins or the EPP fails initialization with an explicit error if an Alpha plugin appears in the config -- currently ALL in-tree plugins are Alpha or Beta, none are Stable, since the project is pre-1.0.
stance_target: operational risk/stability caveat for building on any current llm-d-router plugin, including the multicluster ones cited as non-k8s precedent
quoted_support: Currently, all in-tree plugins are classified as Alpha or Beta. Plugins will be promoted to Stable as the project approaches its 1.0 release.
